problem: Measures EIP-7702 abuse on 7 chains: 924 malicious contract accounts; >63% of 3,664,166 authorizations tied to EOA-targeted attacks; ~$2.36M lost, ~$10.14M exposed; legacy tx.origin==msg.sender checks no longer hold
trust_assumption: Benign users' keys are not stolen; users or wallets approve the authorization
ibs_relation: Evidence for C2 default-deny of delegation and C4 code-at-EOA tripwire; consumer phishing, not custodial orchestration
gap: Does not address custodial signers whose orchestration requests delegations

problem: Shows one phished authorization tuple gives persistent full control; three trigger pathways; first cross-chain usage measurement; protocol-level defenses
trust_assumption: Wallet shows the authorization faithfully; user judges it
ibs_relation: Prior art for the delegation threat; complements C2 (deny 7702 by default)
gap: Consumer phishing; no institutional signing policy or post-sign containment

problem: Reference frame for 181 DeFi incidents (Apr 2018-Apr 2022, $3.24B); 56% of attacks non-atomic (rescue window); 87 of 183 victims had an emergency pause but only 51 paused within 48 h and one within 1 h; compromised key/wallet is an operational-layer cause (22 incidents, 12%) addressed by few papers
ibs_relation: Supports C4 premise twice: a response window exists, and human-triggered pauses are too slow to use it
gap: Custodial key/signing-path incidents out of scope

problem: Systematizes 31 bridge attacks (2021-2023) into 10 vulnerability types; defenses and open problems
ibs_relation: Context for U2 incidents and validator-key compromise; C1 analogue = deposit-evidence binding
gap: Off-chain signer compromise treated as key management, not intent binding

problem: Analyzes 36 Bitcoin exchange breaches with a CTI standard; most due to lax security
ibs_relation: Baseline empirical work on exchange breaches (pre-2020)
gap: Stops before account-abstraction era and signing-request manipulation

problem: Extended breach analysis, security posture of surviving exchanges, laundering of stolen BTC
ibs_relation: Baseline empirical work; laundering context for S4
gap: Bitcoin-only; no signing-path analysis

problem: Four practical key-extraction attacks on threshold-ECDSA (GG18/GG20, Lindell17) implementations used by MPC wallets
ibs_relation: Shows MPC protects the key, not the decision to sign; IBS is orthogonal (sits before the signer)
gap: Does not address an honest MPC quorum signing a malicious but valid request

problem: Per-protocol anomaly models (call-flow model + likely invariants) flag attack transactions in real time: 94.8% TPR (109 of 115 incidents, 22M tx), 0.16% FPR; ~28 ms per detection
trust_assumption: Protocol behaviour models learned from history
post_sign_containment: partial (detects pending or included tx; prevention needs mempool visibility plus a pause or front-run hook)
evaluation: replay of 115 incidents; 20-day live run on 20 protocols (Apr 2024, 0.08% alerts); 3-week rerun (Oct-Nov 2025, 0.07%, no attacks); BSC port (11 of 12)
ibs_relation: Closest academic analogue to C4 for protocols; IBS's watcher targets custodial treasury flows and reconciles against an intent ledger
gap: Protocol contracts, not custodial hot wallets; no intent ledger; filters out plain ETH and standard token transfers, which is the form custodial drains take; blind to private-relay transactions until inclusion

problem: Mempool fuzzer over transaction 'symbols' (future, overdraft, latent overdraft, replacement) finds new asymmetric-DoS bugs in six clients including Besu; DETER bugs fixed in all major clients by Fall 2023
ibs_relation: Closest prior work to E8 and gives its vocabulary: clients admit transactions without executing them, and admission rules for overdraft and latent-overdraft transactions differ by client
gap: DoS focus; does not study how mempool admission changes theft outcomes

problem: Evaluates 53 Ethereum wallets against address poisoning; few warn users
ibs_relation: Display-integrity evidence; consumer wallets
gap: Not custodial; no policy or containment

problem: Six recurring flaws in audited ERC-4337 smart accounts (access control, signature binding, paymasters)
ibs_relation: Shows programmable accounts move risk into account code; relevant if IBS is enforced on-chain
gap: Grey literature; implementation flaws, not signing-path compromise

problem: BitForge: GG18/GG20 Paillier-key flaw allows full key extraction (CVE-2023-33241); many wallets affected
ibs_relation: Same point as makriyannis2023mpcattacks from the vendor side
gap: Grey literature

problem: Wallet design taxonomy; multi-layer attack framework; incident analysis (arXiv v5: 85 incidents 2012-2025, $6.98B; v4: 84 / $5.4B); of 29 defence methods only 7 are remedial and 1 is a response method; Bybit case study
trust_assumption: Varies by wallet type; custodial wallets trust the operator's infrastructure
post_sign_containment: partial (remedial defences catalogued, not evaluated; few exist)
ibs_relation: Evidence base for RQ1; public incident dataset is a second source for our catalog cross-check
gap: Classifies wallet types, not the custodial signing pipeline; no evaluation of defenses against orchestration compromise

problem: Covenants restrict how outputs can be spent; vaults force a publicly visible delay so a stolen key can be countered by a recovery key
trust_assumption: Recovery key stays uncompromised; owner watches the chain during the delay
ibs_relation: Closest prior art for C3+C4: bounded, delayed exposure plus a recovery path
gap: Needs a Bitcoin consensus change; no notion of operation intent; delay applies to every spend, so it suits cold storage, not hot-wallet throughput

problem: Policy-based signatures: a key can only sign messages that satisfy an authority-set policy, and signatures hide the policy
trust_assumption: Authority issuing policy keys is honest; policy fixed at key issuance
ibs_relation: Cryptographic analogue of C2 (deny-by-default policy enforced at signing)
gap: Policy is static per key, not tied to a per-operation intent; non-standard verification, so not usable for ECDSA accounts on-chain

problem: Policy-compliant signatures: a signature is valid only if a global policy over sender and receiver attributes is satisfied
trust_assumption: Central authority sets the policy and issues keys
ibs_relation: Cryptographic analogue of C2 with receiver-aware policy (e.g. who may pay whom)
gap: Same as PBS: static policy, custom verification; no intent binding or containment

problem: First security study of Ethereum txpool designs; low-cost DoS by flawed admission control in all known clients
ibs_relation: Shows txpool admission rules differ by client and matter for security; context for limitation E8
gap: Studies DoS, not how queued underfunded transactions change loss outcomes in a theft

problem: Phishing contracts that look benign under wallet transaction simulation and behave differently on-chain; SimGuard detector; >4,000 contracts, >5,700 victims, ~$3.48M
ibs_relation: Shows a pre-sign preview can be gamed; supports checking the signed operation against intent (C1) and reconciling outcomes after execution (C4)
gap: Consumer wallets; no custodial policy or post-execution containment

problem: Datalog rules model expected cross-chain behaviour and flag anomalies; finds the Ronin and Nomad attack transactions
trust_assumption: Bridge events and rules are complete; detection is after the fact
evaluation: incident analysis (replay of Ronin and Nomad data)
ibs_relation: Prior art for rule-based reconciliation in C4
gap: Detection only; validator-key compromise (Ronin) is found after the loss

problem: End-to-end balance invariant (outflow = inflow - costs) flags every known bridge attack in 20M+ tx; in-line enforcement via report-then-execute (an independent reporter must vouch before the bridge executes)
trust_assumption: Accounting data on both chains is correct and timely
independent_intent: partial (source-chain deposit is the independent record; report-then-execute adds an independent reporter before execution)
post_sign_containment: yes (in-line audit can block unbalanced withdrawals)
evaluation: retrospective analysis (20M+ tx); 10-month live audit of Wormhole (202k tx, 0.05% alerts, all false); report-then-execute prototype on testnets (100 pairs, 3 malicious rejected)
ibs_relation: Strongest prior art for C4 (accounting reconciliation) and, via report-then-execute, for C1's architecture; earlier preprint version inspired Bascule (Cubist, used by Lombard)
gap: Explicitly excludes attacks that move funds straight out of a bridge wallet with a compromised key (no withdrawal step) - the custodial case; live audit uses finalized blocks (~12 min on Ethereum), so detection is minutes, not seconds

problem: Systematic review and empirical comparison of blockchain simulators
ibs_relation: Methodological context for our simulator plus real-client (Besu) design
gap: Simulators target consensus/network performance, not transaction-level security outcomes

problem: Systematic mapping of blockchain simulators: features, inputs, validated metrics; none covers the full range
ibs_relation: Context for E7 (one client) and the sim-to-real comparison
gap: Same focus as above

problem: New transaction type that lets an EOA set delegated code via signed authorization tuples
trust_assumption: Holder of the EOA key signs authorizations knowingly
ibs_relation: Defines the attack surface for A3 and the C2/C4 rules on delegation
gap: Standard itself; security depends on wallets and policy

problem: Account abstraction through UserOperations, bundlers and an EntryPoint contract, without consensus changes
ibs_relation: Context: smart accounts move policy into validation code
gap: Policy in validation code is only as good as what it can see

problem: Interfaces for modular smart accounts: validators, executors, hooks
trust_assumption: Installed modules are correct and not replaced
post_sign_containment: partial (hooks can check before and after execution)
ibs_relation: Hooks are a possible on-chain enforcement point for C2/C3
gap: Module installation is itself a privileged signing action

problem: Standard order format for cross-chain intents filled by solvers
ibs_relation: Terminology only: 'intent' here is a solver-filled order, not an independently authored operation record
gap: Different problem (execution outsourcing)

problem: JSON descriptors so wallets can show contract calls and typed messages in human-readable form (clear signing)
trust_assumption: Descriptor registry, external data sources (token metadata, ENS) and the device display
independent_intent: no (the human compares the display with their own belief)
ibs_relation: Prior art and complement for C1: makes the payload readable at the signer; its own security section names front-end/CDN compromise and registry poisoning, and lists binding frontends to verified manifests as future work
gap: Readable is not the same as intended: nothing checks the call against an intent recorded elsewhere

problem: Protocol-level circuit breaker: delay or revert token outflows once a rate threshold is exceeded
trust_assumption: Thresholds are set well; the operator can't be the attacker
ibs_relation: Prior art for C3 exposure budgets enforced on-chain
gap: DeFi protocol scope; a third-party audit (Zellic) reports complexity and a griefing path; never standardized

problem: Industry control standard for key material: generation, storage, usage (incl. spend verification, multi-signer use), compromise policy, audit logs
independent_intent: partial (spend verification; text still to be read)
ibs_relation: Standards baseline; IBS controls should map onto CCSS aspect 1.05
gap: Process controls; does not specify an independent machine-checkable intent or automatic containment

problem: Technical reconstruction of Bybit: injected Safe{Wallet} UI code sent altered data to hardware wallets; after the attack the Safe gateway began checking that proposal hash and signature match
ibs_relation: Evidence that the proposal-to-signature binding was missing at the orchestration layer (C1 gap)
gap: Single incident; vendor analysis

problem: Reviews 2022-2023 bridge hacks and exploited weaknesses; notes several were caused by poor IT practice rather than on-chain code
ibs_relation: Evidence that bridge losses often come from the operational signing path (U2/U3 scope)
gap: Review only; no defense evaluation

problem: Breaks bridges into components and reviews exploits by component
ibs_relation: Bridge-component vocabulary for U2 incidents
gap: Pre-2023 incidents; no evaluation

problem: Survival analysis of 40 Bitcoin exchanges: 18 closed, 9 breached; high-volume exchanges close less but are breached more
ibs_relation: Foundational evidence that exchange custody is the dominant user risk
gap: Early era; no signing-path detail

problem: Revisits exchange closure risk with 80 exchanges (2010-2015) and quarterly indicators
ibs_relation: Longitudinal baseline for RQ1
gap: Closure risk, not theft mechanics

problem: Tamarin model of the EIP-7702 delegation lifecycle composed with the ERC-4337 EntryPoint; ten machine-checked attack patterns; checks mitigations
trust_assumption: Symbolic model matches client and contract behaviour
ibs_relation: Method we can reuse to formally check C2 delegation rules; independent confirmation of the 7702 attack surface behind A3
gap: Account-level; no custodial orchestration or containment

problem: Identifies and profiles on-chain wallet contracts on Ethereum; groups them into six types (limits, approvals, multisig, recovery)
ibs_relation: Shows which on-chain policy features (daily limits, approvals) wallets actually ship: C3-like budgets exist on-chain
gap: Pre-2021 data; no attack evaluation

problem: Explains ERC-4337 account abstraction and qualitatively assesses its security effect
ibs_relation: Background for RQ5
gap: Qualitative only

problem: PRISMA-ScR review building a dataset of 220 exchange incidents (80 CEX, 140 DEX, 2009-2024, $8.494B); classifies attack vectors; discusses post-quantum risk
ibs_relation: Candidate second source for our catalog cross-check (CEX incidents)
gap: Different inclusion rules and loss sources from ours; per-incident evidence must be checked

problem: Unified description and comparison of threshold ECDSA protocols and open-source implementations
trust_assumption: Protocol assumptions (honest/dishonest majority, correct ZK proofs)
ibs_relation: Background for T2: MPC removes the single key but not the single request path
gap: Signing correctness only: MPC parties sign whatever request the orchestration sends

problem: Key-extraction attacks from implementation flaws in threshold ECDSA libraries
ibs_relation: Evidence that key-layer defenses have their own failure modes; complements makriyannis2023
gap: Key extraction, not request manipulation

problem: Multi-transaction differential fuzzing across Ethereum clients finds consensus bugs; one later split mainnet
trust_assumption: Clients that agree are correct (cross-referencing oracle)
ibs_relation: Method precedent for our cross-backend comparison (Hardhat vs Besu) as a differential oracle
gap: Consensus state, not mempool admission or loss outcomes

problem: Clipboard malware swaps in pre-mined look-alike addresses so users who check only a few characters approve the attacker's address on Trezor, Ledger and KeepKey
trust_assumption: User fully compares the address on the device
ibs_relation: Evidence that human comparison on a trusted display is weak; motivates a machine check against an intent record (C1)
gap: Consumer setting; no institutional controls

problem: Ten-participant study with simulated MITM attacks: most participants caught some but not all address substitutions
ibs_relation: Small but direct evidence that signer-side human verification fails
gap: Very small sample; consumer device

problem: Proposed verification provider simulates and risk-scores a transaction and signs the result; the hardware wallet checks that signature before the user signs
trust_assumption: Provider key and risk model; user still judges intent
independent_intent: partial (independent party, but checks risk, not intent)
ibs_relation: Closest industry design to C1's architecture (a second trust domain attests the request before signing); differs because it attests safety, not a recorded intent
gap: No intent record, so a 'safe-looking' but unintended transfer passes; simulation can be gamed (wang2026simphishing)

problem: AI risk score on simulated transactions; high-risk transactions are dropped before the rollup sequencer
trust_assumption: Model recall; operator controls the sequencer
post_sign_containment: partial (blocks before inclusion; no post-execution reconciliation)
ibs_relation: Industry analogue of pre-execution screening; contrast with C4, which reconciles what landed against intent
gap: Works where the operator controls ordering (rollups); not available on a public L1 for a custodian's own withdrawals

problem: On-chain role-based permissions for Safe: allowlisted targets, functions, parameter conditions and allowances; optional delay module for veto
trust_assumption: Policy authors and the Safe owners who install it
post_sign_containment: partial (delay modifier gives a veto window)
ibs_relation: Deployed on-chain counterpart of C2 (deny-by-default scoping) and C3 (allowances)
gap: Changing the policy is itself a Safe transaction, so the Bybit-style manipulated-request attack applies to policy updates

problem: Compromised npm account shipped a drainer in Ledger Connect Kit 1.1.5-1.1.7; unpinned CDN loading spread it to many dApps
ibs_relation: Evidence for the U3 path: signing UIs load code that the signer device cannot vet
gap: Below the $10M catalog threshold; consumer users

problem: Banking rule (PSD2 SCA) that the authentication code for a remote payment must be specific to the amount and payee the payer agreed to, and any change invalidates it
trust_assumption: Payer sees the true amount and payee; channel integrity
independent_intent: partial (binds the authorization to amount and payee, but the payer's own view is the reference)
ibs_relation: Regulatory precedent for C1 in traditional payments: authorization cryptographically tied to what was agreed
gap: No crypto-asset equivalent; for custodians the 'payer' is an internal process, so the agreed amount and payee must come from an independent record

problem: Privacy-preserving proof that an exchange's reserves cover customer liabilities
trust_assumption: Exchange publishes proofs honestly and regularly
post_sign_containment: partial (reveals a shortfall after the fact)
ibs_relation: Adjacent to C4: an accounting check that would show the result of a theft, not stop it
gap: Periodic, not real-time; says nothing about which withdrawal was unauthorized

problem: Signer recomputes the EIP-712 Safe transaction hash on a separate machine and compares it with the hardware wallet display
trust_assumption: The data fed to the tool is correct; by default it is fetched from the same Safe transaction service the attacker may control
independent_intent: partial (independent only when the signer enters the intended transaction by hand)
ibs_relation: Human-operated version of C1: compare the signed hash with an independently computed one
gap: Manual, per-signer, and only as independent as its input; no policy or containment

problem: 2FA for smart-contract wallets: short air-gapped OTPs verified against the blockchain, protecting against a stolen key, a stolen authenticator or a tampered client
trust_assumption: The authenticator device and the wallet contract
independent_intent: partial (second factor from a separate device, not an operation record)
ibs_relation: Prior art for C1's separate-domain confirmation in self-custody; on-chain enforcement
gap: Per-user second factor; no institutional intent record, budgets bound to signing, or containment

problem: Classifies wallets by which authentication factors are verified against the blockchain versus locally or by a central party
ibs_relation: Vocabulary for where IBS's check sits (a centrally verified factor before signing)
gap: Authentication of the user, not whether a request matches an intent

problem: Systematic review of wallet attack surfaces in six layers (memory/storage, OS, software, network, protocol, user) and countermeasures
ibs_relation: Coverage check for T9 endpoint attacks on signers
gap: Wallet-software focus; institutional signing pipelines not covered

problem: Models each key as safe, lost, leaked or stolen and finds the wallet (key combination) with the lowest failure probability
trust_assumption: Key-state probabilities are independent and known
evaluation: formal (probabilistic model, exhaustive and evolutionary search)
ibs_relation: Background for multisig thresholds (A5's 2-of-3 with S as co-signer)
gap: Keys only; a compromised request path is not a key state

problem: First security model for hot/cold (deterministic) wallets and a provably secure ECDSA-based scheme
ibs_relation: Background: hot/cold separation that IBS sits in front of
gap: Key derivation, not request authorization

problem: Design of a chain-agnostic 2-of-3 MPC-TSS shared-custodial wallet for wealth managers, with distributed key management and recovery
trust_assumption: MPC parties and the custodian's application
ibs_relation: Custody architecture context for T2
gap: Design only; no signing-request verification against intent

problem: Shows desktop wallets' local RPC interfaces let other users on the same computer steal funds; current authentication is insufficient
ibs_relation: Endpoint evidence: the signing interface itself is an attack surface
gap: Single-user wallets

problem: HSM prototype managing the life cycle of Ethereum keys and transaction signing
trust_assumption: The HSM and whoever submits requests to it
ibs_relation: Background: an HSM signs whatever its caller sends, the gap C1 addresses
gap: Key protection only

problem: Measures real-world attacks and deployed defences from 420M Ethereum transactions (2015-2019); finds defences evaded through incomplete deployment
post_sign_containment: partial (observes deployed defences that blocked attempts)
ibs_relation: Evidence that deployed defences have gaps in practice
gap: Contract exploits, not custodial signing

problem: FrontDef: detects malicious flash-loan attack transactions in the mempool and front-runs them with replica transactions
trust_assumption: Attack is visible in the public mempool before inclusion
ibs_relation: Contrast for C4 and T5: pre-inclusion response needs a public mempool; private or atomic submissions defeat it
gap: Protocol attacks; a custodian's drain need not pass the public mempool

problem: Dual-gate MPC custody: separates member authentication from threshold authorization so the signature scheme can change (post-quantum)
trust_assumption: Fewer than t custody parties compromised
ibs_relation: Shows authorization logic can be programmable inside custody; budgets mentioned as richer policies
gap: No intent record or containment

problem: PASS: provenance-based access for shared wallets; a subaccount may spend only assets it can trace to a deposit; Lean 4 proofs; TEE prototype
trust_assumption: The TEE holding the key and its light client
independent_intent: partial (provenance acts as an independent record of entitlement)
ibs_relation: Related to C1/C3: a machine-checked entitlement rule at the signer
gap: Entitlement by provenance, not intent; TEE trust

problem: User-signed open Mandates state constraints (amount range, payees, budget, recurrence); agents sign closed Mandates that verifiers check against them
trust_assumption: The user's Trusted Surface and the verifiers (merchant, credential provider)
independent_intent: yes (constraints authored on a trusted surface, checked by machine before payment credentials are released)
ibs_relation: Closest standard to C1 outside custody; its budget adds an amount at approval, and an agent must not present a new open Mandate before a rejection receipt for the previous one
gap: Commerce payments, not a custodian's own outbound transfers; no containment

problem: JSON-RPC for dapps to request scoped execution permissions (e.g. token allowances with expiry) that the account enforces via ERC-7710 delegation
trust_assumption: The wallet that grants and the on-chain delegation manager
ibs_relation: On-chain allowances count at execution; contrast for C3's signer-side counting
gap: Consumer sessions; no intent record

problem: New transaction type with expire_by block number; expired transactions must not execute or propagate
ibs_relation: Chain-level alternative to the hoarding fix: a held signature would expire; stagnant, so not available
gap: Not adopted

problem: EAS attestations that a reviewer checked an ERC-7730 clear-signing descriptor with a given hash
trust_assumption: Attesters the wallet chooses to trust
ibs_relation: Hardens the descriptor registry that erc7730 depends on
gap: Display integrity; does not tie the request to an independent intent; explicitly excludes malicious attesters and semantic attacks

problem: On-chain registry where an authorized attestor issues a per-action, transaction-scoped attestation (capability + action digest) and executes the action atomically
independent_intent: partial (an off-chain attestor evaluates each action; semantics left to upper layers)
ibs_relation: Related to C1: per-operation gating by a separate party, enforced on-chain
gap: Agent actions; attestor logic unspecified; no budgets or containment

problem: Launch of the Clear Signing standard and registry (ERC-7730 descriptors, attested under ERC-8176)
trust_assumption: Descriptor authors and attesters; wallets choose sources
ibs_relation: Update to the display layer in O1
gap: Same residual trust as erc7730: the human and the descriptor

problem: Customer-hosted Callback Handler receives every signing or approval request from the API Co-signer and must APPROVE before the Co-signer joins MPC signing
independent_intent: yes (architecture: a separate, customer-run check by machine before signing); what it checks is customer-defined
ibs_relation: Direct prior art for C1's placement; IBS must specify what is checked and evaluate it
gap: Optional; check logic unspecified and unevaluated in public; no containment

problem: Webhook policy rule sends each triggering transaction to the customer's server; non-200 denies or escalates; velocity limits over a time window
trust_assumption: The customer's webhook server; BitGo's policy engine
ibs_relation: Prior art for C1 placement and C3 velocity limits; counting time for velocity not stated
gap: Check logic customer-defined; recovery transactions bypass policies by design

problem: After the Triple-A incident, argues for independent intent verification by callbacks in the client's own trust domain, fail-closed, before signature generation
trust_assumption: Separation of trust domains between business systems and signing nodes
ibs_relation: States C1's principle in industry terms; supports the threat model
gap: No public evaluation; vendor perspective

problem: Policy engine with velocity limits; claims every policy evaluation runs inside the MPC signing path
ibs_relation: Counter-example to chen2026bts's claim that deployed limits always sit outside signing; unverified
gap: Marketing claim; counting rule not stated

problem: Shows how any Safe can be backdoored at deployment (setup delegatecall, modules) so accounts other than the owners control it
ibs_relation: Evidence for C2 treating delegatecall and modules as high-risk
gap: Deployment-time, not signing-time

problem: Contracts detect transaction simulation (e.g. COINBASE set to zero) and behave benignly only in simulation; six vendors affected and fixed
ibs_relation: Evidence that pre-sign simulation is a risk model, not an intent (O1)
gap: Consumer wallets
